name: Refrigerator Door Shelf Bin
description: Manufacturer-certified refrigerator door shelf bin (also called a door bin). Clear plastic with white trim, used to hold jars, bottles, cans, and condiments in the fridge door. Tool-free, snap-in installation.

steps: Open the refrigerator door fully to access the bin.
Tilt the front of the old bin upward to release it from the door rails.
Lift the bin up and out of the door liner.
Align the new bin with the molded rails on the door liner.
Press down and back until the bin snaps securely into place.
Tug gently to confirm the bin is locked before loading items.

name: Refrigerator Water Filter (EveryDrop Filter 1)
description: Genuine refrigerator water filter that reduces contaminants, chlorine taste, and odor. Should be replaced about every 6 months for clean water and ice.

steps: Locate the filter (usually in the upper-right interior or in the base grille).
Turn the old filter a quarter-turn counter-clockwise and pull it out.
Remove the cap from the old filter and place it on the new filter if required.
Insert the new filter and turn a quarter-turn clockwise until it locks.
Run about 3 gallons of water through the dispenser to clear air and carbon fines.
Reset the filter indicator light if your model has one.

name: Refrigerator Ice Maker Assembly
description: Complete modular ice maker assembly. Replace when the ice maker stops producing ice, makes hollow or undersized cubes, or fails to eject ice even though water reaches the unit.

steps: Unplug the refrigerator or switch off the breaker before starting.
Turn the ice maker off and empty the ice bin.
Remove the two mounting screws and the wiring harness plug from the old ice maker.
Lift the old ice maker out of the freezer compartment.
Connect the wiring harness to the new ice maker assembly.
Mount the new ice maker with the screws and align the fill cup with the water inlet.
Restore power and allow up to 24 hours for the first full ice harvest.

name: Refrigerator Water Inlet Valve
description: Dual water inlet valve that controls water flow to the ice maker and water dispenser. A failed valve is a common cause of an ice maker that gets power but produces no ice.

steps: Unplug the refrigerator and shut off the household water supply to the fridge.
Pull the refrigerator away from the wall and remove the rear access panel.
Place a towel under the valve and disconnect the water lines (mark each line).
Unplug the electrical connectors and remove the mounting screw.
Mount the new valve, reconnect the water lines, and confirm they are seated.
Reconnect the electrical plugs, restore water and power, and check for leaks.

name: Refrigerator Defrost Thermostat
description: Defrost thermostat that monitors evaporator temperature and allows the defrost heater to run. A failed thermostat causes frost buildup and warm fridge temperatures.

steps: Unplug the refrigerator and empty the freezer.
Remove the freezer rear panel to expose the evaporator coils.
Locate the defrost thermostat clipped to the coil and unplug it.
Clip the new thermostat onto the coil in the same position.
Reconnect the wiring and reinstall the rear panel.
Restore power and verify the fridge cools normally over 24 hours.

name: Refrigerator Crisper Drawer
description: Clear humidity-controlled crisper drawer for storing fruits and vegetables. Slides on the lower refrigerator rails.

steps: Pull the drawer out to its full extension.
Lift the front of the drawer slightly and pull it free of the rails.
Set the new drawer onto the rails at the same angle.
Slide the drawer fully closed to confirm smooth travel.

name: Refrigerator Door Gasket (Seal)
description: Magnetic door gasket that seals the refrigerator door. A torn or hardened gasket lets cold air escape, causing the compressor to run constantly and sweat to form.

steps: Soak the new gasket in warm water to relax it for easier fitting.
Peel back the old gasket to expose the retaining screws and loosen them.
Remove the old gasket and tuck the new gasket's lip behind the retainer.
Hand-tighten the screws, working from the top corners down.
Use a hair dryer to smooth any waves, then close the door to check the seal.

name: Refrigerator Temperature Control Board
description: Main electronic control board that manages cooling, defrost cycles, and the ice maker. Suspect the board when multiple systems behave erratically.

steps: Unplug the refrigerator before servicing electronics.
Remove the rear access panel covering the control board housing.
Photograph the wiring, then unplug each connector from the old board.
Release the board from its housing clips and remove it.
Seat the new board, reconnect every connector per your photo, and reinstall the panel.
Restore power and confirm normal operation.

name: Dishwasher Drain Pump
description: Drain pump that removes water from the dishwasher tub at the end of a cycle. Replace when the dishwasher won't drain, leaves standing water, or hums without pumping.

steps: Disconnect power and shut off the water supply to the dishwasher.
Remove the lower dish rack and the bottom spray arm and filter.
Pull the dishwasher out and tip it back to access the pump underneath (towel the floor).
Disconnect the wiring and the drain hose from the old pump.
Twist the old pump off the sump and remove it.
Twist the new pump into the sump, reconnect the hose and wiring, and check the seal.
Restore power and water, then run a rinse cycle to confirm it drains.

name: Dishwasher Door Seal (Gasket)
description: Door seal/gasket (about 71 inches, stretches to ~75) that keeps water inside the tub. Replace when water leaks from the door during a wash cycle.

steps: Open the dishwasher door and locate the channel around the tub opening.
Pull the old gasket out of the channel, starting at one corner.
Soak the new gasket in warm water for a few minutes to soften it.
Press the center top of the new gasket into the channel first, then work down both sides.
Push the remaining gasket evenly into the channel without stretching it.
Close the door and run a short cycle to confirm there is no leak.

name: Dishwasher Lower Dishrack Wheel Assembly
description: Gray lower dishrack wheel assembly that lets the bottom rack roll in and out. Four are typically used per dishwasher. Replace cracked or missing wheels that make the rack drag.

steps: Pull the lower rack all the way out and lift it free of the tracks.
Locate the wheel clip on the rack frame.
Squeeze the clip and pull the old wheel off the post.
Push the new wheel onto the post until the clip snaps.
Set the rack back on its tracks and confirm it rolls smoothly.

name: Dishwasher Upper Rack Adjuster Kit
description: Upper rack adjuster kit with white wheels. Includes left and right adjusters and all components to service the upper rack. Newer kits upgrade the part from plastic to metal.

steps: Pull the upper rack out and release the rack stops to remove it from the tracks.
Unclip the old adjuster assemblies from both sides of the rack.
Attach the new left and right adjusters, matching the labeled sides.
Reinstall the wheels and slide the rack back onto the tracks.
Reattach the rack stops and verify the rack raises and lowers evenly.

name: Dishwasher Lower Spray Arm
description: Lower spray arm that sprays water over the bottom rack. Clogged or cracked spray arms are a leading cause of dishes coming out dirty.

steps: Remove the lower dish rack to expose the spray arm.
Unthread or unclip the retaining nut at the center of the spray arm.
Lift the old spray arm straight up off the hub.
Seat the new spray arm on the hub and secure the retaining nut.
Spin the arm by hand to confirm it rotates freely before running a cycle.

name: Dishwasher Filter (Triple Filter / Screen)
description: Fine filter / screen that traps food particles so they are not redeposited on dishes. A clogged filter causes gritty residue and poor cleaning.

steps: Remove the lower rack to access the filter at the bottom of the tub.
Twist the upper cylindrical filter a quarter-turn counter-clockwise and lift it out.
Lift out the lower fine filter screen.
Rinse the area, then set the new fine filter screen in place.
Insert the upper filter and twist clockwise until it locks.
Confirm both filters are seated flush before running a cycle.

name: Dishwasher Silverware Basket
description: Replacement silverware basket for the lower rack. Swap out when the basket cracks or the lid tabs break.

steps: Open the lower rack and lift out the old silverware basket.
Place the new basket in the same position on the rack.
Confirm the basket sits flat and the lids open and close freely.

name: Dishwasher Detergent Dispenser Assembly
description: Detergent dispenser assembly mounted in the door. Replace when the dispenser door won't open during the cycle or detergent is left behind.

steps: Disconnect power to the dishwasher.
Open the door and remove the screws around the inner door panel.
Separate the inner door panel to expose the dispenser and its wiring.
Unplug the dispenser connector and release the mounting clips.
Install the new dispenser, reconnect the wiring, and reassemble the door panel.
Restore power and run a cycle to confirm the dispenser opens.

name: Dishwasher Mounting Bracket
description: Upper mounting bracket that secures the dishwasher to the underside of the counter to stop it from rocking or tipping when the door opens. Sold individually, without screws.

steps: Open the dishwasher door to expose the top mounting tabs.
Slide the new bracket into the slot on the top of the tub.
Push the dishwasher fully into the cabinet opening.
Drive the mounting screws up into the underside of the countertop.
Close the door and confirm the dishwasher no longer tips.
